profile: steady FrameTee hold/release and immediate queue consumption
build: cargo test -p kardamom-engine --lib --release --locked steady_tee_profile -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1; repository thin LTO, codegen-units=1
baseline: 70d57d7a (production reader files only; identical manual profile in both test binaries)
comparison: checked restart history forwarding; no steady FrameTee state added
method: Five paired repeats, alternating execution order, same CPU affinity (CPU 0), 2000 warmup frames and 20000 timed frames per repeat. Every sample includes hold, release and consumer receive. Whole-phase throughput includes per-sample clocks and collection.
conclusion: No observed steady tee latency or throughput regression in controlled repeats. No speedup claim. These are local frame timings, not full client or deployed chain performance.
limitations: Short local samples on a shared host. An initial unpinned pair varied from p50 120 to 160 ns; alternating pinned repeats remove that difference.
Extra checked-history publications occur during restart. Deployed recovery traffic and full client p50/p95/p99, throughput, lag and fallback volume remain unvalidated.
